newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore HSFO seen steady to higher on firm bids.
newsitem.headline: Singapore HSFO seen steady to higher on firm bids.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil prices on Friday were expected to move up on crude gains and strong bids from a handful of buyers, traders said.
One buyer already emerged in late afternoon trading at $117 per tonne free-on-board Singapore, lifting November 26-30 for 20,000 tonnes of 180 cst.
High sulphur 180-cst fuel oil prices were assessed at $113-$115 per tonne on Thursday and were expected to move even higher later Friday.
"A few buyers are keeping prices up," said a European major.
Another trader said two local traders and a Japanese buyer were likely to keep prices supported.
Traders said while supplies were adequate to meet demand, crude gains would help keep the upward momentum intact.
They said China's return to the market for December cargoes would also help support prices.
In the swaps market, December paper was bid/asked at $117.25/$118, little moved from Thursday's quotes.
